gloss: to feel dizzy; to be extremely busy

definitions.gloss: to feel dizzy; to have one's head spin
definitions.explanation: A physical sensation of dizziness or vertigo, as if things are spinning around.

definitions.gloss: to be extremely busy; to be swamped
definitions.explanation: Figuratively describes being so overwhelmed with work or tasks that one's head spins.

examples.japanese: {急|きゅう}に{立|た}ったら{目|め}が{回|まわ}った。
examples.english: I felt dizzy when I stood up suddenly.

examples.japanese: {高|たか}いところから{下|した}を{見|み}ると{目|め}が{回|まわ}る。
examples.english: Looking down from a high place makes me dizzy.

examples.japanese: {乗|の}り{物酔|ものよ}いで{目|め}が{回|まわ}って、{歩|ある}けなかった。
examples.english: I was so dizzy from motion sickness that I couldn't walk.

examples.japanese: {年末|ねんまつ}は{目|め}が{回|まわ}るほど{忙|いそが}しい。
examples.english: The end of the year is dizzyingly busy.

examples.japanese: {注文|ちゅうもん}が{殺到|さっとう}して{目|め}が{回|まわ}る。
examples.english: Orders are flooding in and I'm swamped.

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しの{準備|じゅんび}やら{手続|てつづ}きやらで、{目|め}が{回|まわ}るような{毎日|まいにち}だ。
examples.english: Between moving preparations and paperwork, every day is a whirlwind.

notes:
A common idiomatic expression using the body part {目|め} (eye). The literal image of eyes spinning works for both physical dizziness and figurative overwhelm. Sense 2 often appears in the pattern {目|め}が{回|まわ}るほど{忙|いそが}しい (so busy one's head spins).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {目|め}が{回|まわ}るほど: to the point of dizziness; extremely (busy, etc.)
- {目|め}が{回|まわ}るような{忙|いそが}しさ: dizzying busyness

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- めまいがする: to feel dizzy — more clinical/medical
- {頭|あたま}がくらくらする: head is spinning — more casual
- {猫|ねこ}の{手|て}も{借|か}りたい: so busy one would borrow a cat's paws — idiomatic for extreme busyness
